idiom_name: dict registry keyed by header value + pydantic model_validate
implementation_notes: The registry collapses into a plain dict {token: callable}, which is the local idiom, and the property channel comes from the client (confluent-kafka's Message.headers, pika's BasicProperties.headers). Pydantic v2 can express dispatch too, but only over a payload field: Field(discriminator='pet_type') makes validation pick exactly one union member from a field inside the data, and an untagged union falls back to trying members in order - both are the content-based sibling. The property-based form reads the header, resolves the parser, and only then validates the body.
pitfalls: Header values are bytes and may repeat, so dict(msg.headers()) silently keeps the last one - which can differ from the value the broker used to route.
Letting an untagged union 'guess' turns a mislabelled header into a wrong-but-valid object; a discriminated lookup is what makes the failure loud.
json.loads hooks (object_hook, parse_float) only see the payload, so no stdlib hook can implement header-driven dispatch.
